summary: Free plan card text '30 queries/day' disagrees with FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT (10)
description:
The Free plan card on /account hardcodes "30 queries/day" as a feature bullet, but nothing in the codebase backs that number. The actual server-enforced limit is FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT = 10 (src/lib/pricing-config.ts:49). User reported seeing the card text say "30 queries/day" while their Usage Today panel showed "0 / 100" — the 100 is correct for their current tier (PRO_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT, src/lib/pricing-config.ts:50), but the "30" is a stale/wrong literal.

Source of the bug:

  src/app/(app)/account/page.tsx:11
    { id: 'free', name: 'Free', price: null,
      features: ['30 queries/day', 'All traditions', 'Standard model'] },

Fix:

  1. Import the real constants in page.tsx:
       import { FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT, PRO_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT }
         from '@/lib/pricing-config';

  2. Build the features list from those constants instead of
     hardcoded strings:
       free: \`\${FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT} queries/day\`
       pro:  'Unlimited queries' is also a lie — the soft cap
              is PRO_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT (100). Decide: keep
              "Unlimited queries" for marketing (the cap is a
              runaway-loop guard, not a quota in the user-facing
              sense) OR show the real number. Recommend keeping
              "Unlimited queries" since BRD §6.2 calls the Pro
              cap "a soft secondary gate against runaway loops"
              and the binding gate is USD, not queries — but
              flag this for the implementer to confirm.

  3. Verify no other page hardcodes "30 queries/day" or any
     other quota string. Likely candidates: marketing/landing
     page, FAQ, signup flow.

Done when:
  - /account Free card shows "10 queries/day" (or whatever
    FREE_DAILY_QUERY_LIMIT is at build time).
  - Changing the constant in pricing-config.ts changes the
    displayed text without touching account/page.tsx.
  - tsc + lint + build clean.

Spec: live user feedback during pre-launch cleanup; BRD §6.2 for
the soft-cap rationale on Pro.
